title: Compact AWD Crossover Shortlist

buyer.role: Main family car, with a rear-facing car seat by spring
criteria: Sample data: every model, price, rating and dealer on this page is made up.
Fits a rear-facing seat behind a 6'1" driver
Under 184 inches long, to fit the current garage spot

notes: Taxes and fees are a state-level estimate for an example state: 9.5% vehicle sales tax plus about $700 for title, registration and doc fee. Local taxes and any yearly property tax aren't included.
Prices are at asking. None of these dealers was assumed to negotiate.
Insurance comes from example quotes. Maintenance is priced at shop rates.

sources.title: Example: AAA state gas price average

constraint.name: Car Seat Fit
constraint.intro: A rear-facing seat behind a tall driver is the test that rules cars out. Measurements are second-row legroom and the seat-to-seatback gap with the driver's seat set for a 6'1" driver.

models.name: Northline Compact
models.spectrumNote: A reliable appliance. Proven engine, conventional automatic, cheap parts.
models.repairsNote: Range $300 to $900: mostly brakes and a battery.
models.resaleNote: Example curve: about 42% loss over 5 years from today's fair value.
story: The Northline is the safe answer. It's a third-year design with an engine that has been in production for a decade.
It won't excite you, but it will start every morning and cost the least to own.

failureModes.why: A software bug in early units
failureModes.status: Ask the dealer if it was applied

reviews.title: Example review
reviews.summary: Comfortable, efficient, forgettable to drive. Strong reliability record.

inspection: Check rear tire wear for alignment
walkAway: Any accident with frame or airbag work

models.name: Ardent Wagon
models.spectrumNote: Middle of the road. More fun to drive, with one known weak point.
models.priceNote: Asking at a traditional dealer. Target $27,900.
models.repairsNote: Range $600 to $2,200: water pump risk plus brakes.
models.resaleNote: Example curve: about 45% loss over 5 years.
story: The Ardent is the enthusiast pick. It steers and rides better than the other two, and the wagon body holds more than its size suggests.
The catch is a water pump that fails early on this engine. It's a known, priced risk.

failureModes.why: Plastic housing cracks with heat cycles

reviews.title: Example review
reviews.summary: The driver's choice in the class. Watch the cooling system.

inspection: Look for pink crust at the water pump
walkAway: Coolant loss or a sweet smell
Dealer won't put the CPO terms in writing

models.name: Vela Premium
models.spectrumNote: Premium value with a maintenance tax. The most car for the money, and the most risk.
models.repairsNote: Range $1,500 to $4,500: air suspension and electronics.
models.resaleNote: Example curve: about 57% loss over 5 years.
story: The Vela is the nicest car here by a wide margin. It also has no warranty left and an air suspension that ages badly in salted winters.
It fails your stated priority of a low-drama main car, so it's here as a benchmark.

failureModes.why: Bladders crack with age and road salt

reviews.title: Example review
reviews.summary: Luxurious and quiet. Owners report suspension costs after year five.

inspection: Check that the car sits level after parking overnight

listings.notes: Ask for the water pump to be done before delivery.
41 days on market, one price drop. Front pads at 4 mm.

summary: Three CPO and used crossovers made the shortlist. The Northline Compact costs the least to own over 5 years, insurance included, and clears every criterion.
The Ardent Wagon is the better drive, but its asking price runs $375 over the budget and it carries a known water pump risk. The Vela Premium is the nicest car here and the most expensive to keep.
Next: send the opening offer on the Northline, and book a test drive with the car seat.

negotiation.intro: Targets come from six comparable listings within 50 miles. Negotiate the out-the-door price in writing before visiting.

levers.evidence: Example Motors West has the same trim at $26,900 with 6,600 more miles.
The one-price store won't move on price. Ask for the 7-day return in writing and a fresh set of wiper blades and cabin filter before delivery.

script: I'm ready to buy this week. Comparable cars within 50 miles list from $25,900 to $27,400.
I can do $25,600 plus tax, title and plates. Please send a written out-the-door quote.

levers.evidence: The water pump hasn't been replaced. Ask the dealer to do it before delivery, or take $1,100 off.
Listed 52 days with one price drop.

script: I like the car, but it needs the water pump done, a $900 to $1,300 job on this engine.
I can do $27,200 out the door before fees, or $28,000 with the pump replaced before delivery.

firstYear.intro: Built for the Northline Compact at 18,200 miles, from the example factory schedule and the car's records. Example values only.
first30: Title, registration and any local sticker, by the deadlines in the locale research.
Register the CPO warranty with the maker.
Record a baseline: tread by position, pad thickness, battery test and a code scan.
Get the second key and the owner's manual if the car came without them.

schedule.why: No record of either. A cheap redo beats a guess.
Fixes the known reboot bug if it wasn't applied.
Records show no flush. Factory interval 3 years.

schedule.task: Oil and filter, tire rotation, inspection

paragraphs: Buy the Northline Compact. It has the lowest 5-year cost by about $6,400, fits the car seat with room to spare, and carries the longest warranty runway.
Pick the Ardent Wagon only if the test drive wins you over, and only with the water pump done first and the price near $27,900.
avoid: The Vela Premium: no warranty left and a known four-figure suspension bill, on a car that has to be reliable.
